chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Salih from Abd al-Malik ibn Amr from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The borrower of a loaned item is not liable for its loss, unless the owner stipulates otherwise, except for dirhams (coins), for they are liable whether the owner stipulated or not.

key_terms.الْعَارِيَّة: Loan of an item for use without compensation

ai.seo_question: Is a borrower liable for losing a borrowed item in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* delineates the principle of *qabd* (possession) in loan contracts, establishing that the borrower is generally exempt from liability for accidental loss unless a specific guarantee is stipulated. It highlights a key juristic distinction where coins (*dirhams*) are treated as *damin* (liable) by default due to their fungible nature as currency, unlike other items which require explicit stipulation for liability. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the intrinsic characteristics of the loaned object in determining risk allocation.
